## AIBehaviourBase

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIBehaviourBase.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The base for one AI behaviour, such as Wander or Chase: one concrete thing to do.

A child of the pawn's [`AIBehaviourManager`](#aibehaviourmanager), which only judges between behaviours. Its settings come from its `definition`, shared by every pawn using it ([`AIBehaviourDefinition`](#aibehaviourdefinition)); empty, it runs with its kind's defaults. It acts only through the AI controller (`context.controller.move_to()`, `press()`), never on abilities or the body. Extend it: `make_default_definition()` for settings of its own, then `own_conditions()`, `enter()`, `tick()` (return SUCCEEDED or FAILED to finish) and `exit()`. Its node name is its name: the fixed order and the random numbers read it. Settings in ticks are written for 60 a second. Design: pawn spec 10.7 and 16.3, scaling spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `enabled: bool` = `true`: Off: never chosen, and a running one is replaced, as if it weren't there. The way an inherited scene switches off a behaviour it can't remove.
- `definition: AIBehaviourDefinition`: The settings it runs with: a file shared by every pawn that uses it, or one embedded in this node while prototyping. Empty: its kind's defaults. One of another kind falls back to the defaults, with a warning.
- `settings: AIBehaviourDefinition` = `null`: The settings it runs with: `definition` worked out, or its kind's defaults, with anything written on the node on top. Read-only while playing. Set by `prepare_settings()`.
- `manager: AIBehaviourManager` = `null`: Set by the AIBehaviourManager.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this behaviour belongs to. Set by the AIBehaviourManager.
- `name_hash: int` = `0`: Worked out once by the manager: a hash of the name, for random numbers.
- `started_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick it last started (-1: never).
- `ended_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick it last ended (-1: never).
- `perf_available_name: StringName` = `&""`: The timing scope names for its is_available() and its tick(), such as &"ai.available.Chase" and &"ai.behaviour.Chase" (see [`PerfScopes`](../diagnostics/REFERENCE.md#perfscopes)). Made once by the manager, so timing makes no new names.
- `perf_tick_name: StringName` = `&""`: The timing scope name for its tick(), such as &"ai.behaviour.Chase". Made once by the manager.
- `modifier_changes: PackedFloat64Array[]` = `[]`: What the behaviour modifiers that count for it do to each of its numbers (`AIBehaviourModifier.Number`): one `[multiply, add, overrides, override value]` per number. Worked out by the manager when they or the owned tags change.
- `decision_blocked: bool` = `false`: A blocking behaviour modifier counts for it. Set by the manager with `modifier_changes`.
- `decision_bonus: float` = `0.0`
- `decision_jitter: float` = `0.0`
- `decision_ceiling: float` = `0.0`
- `decision_floor: float` = `0.0`
- `decision_available: bool` = `false`
- `availability_checked: bool` = `false`
- `decision_score: float` = `0.0`
- `decision_scored: bool` = `false`
- `decision_index: int` = `0`
- `warned_score_range: bool` = `false`
- `wake_tick: int` = `-1`: Wake-ups, read by the manager (see the class description). Cleared when it starts.
- `wakes_on_path_end: bool` = `false`
- `wakes_on_action: StringName` = `&""`
- `woken: bool` = `false`

### Constants

- `Status.RUNNING = 0`
- `Status.SUCCEEDED = 1`
- `Status.FAILED = 2`

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`: The definition a new node of this kind runs with: a new definition of the kind's class, with its defaults. Each kind overrides it.
- `prepare_settings() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`: Works out `settings` from `definition`, with settings written on the node on top. Called as it's made, when its definition changes, after a setting is written on it, and by the manager as it collects its behaviours. Returns the settings.
- `use_definition(new_definition: AIBehaviourDefinition) -> void`: Gives it another definition while playing. Behaviours can change in play (the AI runs on the server and never rolls back): the manager works out its inputs again and C++ gets the new brain.
- `make_definition_unique() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`: Gives it settings of its own, on top of its definition, which this node alone uses: Godot's "Make Unique", while playing. Its settings can be written after that. For prototyping and tests; a shipped game uses another definition or a behaviour modifier.
- `has_own_settings() -> bool`: True if it has settings of its own on top of its definition (`make_definition_unique()`, or values a scene sets on the node).
- `definition_note() -> String`: Where its settings come from, for diagnostics: "fell back", "embedded", "own settings" or "" (`DefinitionSettings.note()`).
- `is_available(context: AIManager) -> bool`: Its own yes or no, after the manager's checks: every condition passes (`all_conditions()`). The inputs they read were worked out for this decision by the behaviour manager. Overriding this with code works, but see `has_own_code()`.
- `score(context: AIManager) -> float`: How much it wants to run now, between min_score and max_score: max_score, scaled by `score_curves` if it has any.
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: The conditions it builds from its own settings, such as Attack's reach. Override in a behaviour script; the default: none. Called once, the first time they're needed, and again after `rebuild_conditions()`.
- `all_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: Its own conditions, then the ones in `conditions`: everything `is_available()` checks by default.
- `rebuild_conditions() -> void`: Builds the conditions again at the next decision, after a setting they come from changed (such as a swing's reach).
- `add_input_slots(slots: Dictionary) -> void`: Adds the slots of every input its conditions and curves read to slots (as keys).
- `has_own_code() -> bool`: True if its script overrides `is_available()` or `score()` with code of its own. Such a behaviour works everywhere, but the C++ decider can't read code, so it asks GDScript for that behaviour's answers. Worked out once per script ([`ScriptOverrides`](../platform/REFERENCE.md#scriptoverrides)).
- `judged_in_gdscript() -> bool`: True if the C++ decider can't judge it from data: it has code of its own (`has_own_code()`) or a condition of a kind C++ doesn't read (`AICondition.cpp_reads()`). GDScript then answers for this behaviour at each C++ decision; C++ judges the rest.
- `check_score_range(raw: float) -> void`: Warns once (debug builds) if a score its score() gave is outside min_score to max_score: the manager skips behaviours by those bounds, so choices may be wrong. Both deciders call it with each score they get from GDScript.
- `wake_at(at_tick: int) -> void`: Runs tick() at this tick (or the pawn's first run after it), if nothing wakes it sooner. Used up when it fires; an earlier tick than one already set wins.
- `wake_on_path_end() -> void`: Runs tick() when a walk it started ends, arrived or given up (PathFollower.path_ended, on the AI controller's follower).
- `wake_on_action_end(action: StringName) -> void`: Runs tick() when an ability on this action finishes or is cancelled (AbilityManager.ability_finished, ability_cancelled).
- `clear_wake_ups() -> void`: Forgets every wake-up. The manager calls it when the behaviour starts.
- `enter(_context: AIManager) -> void`: Once, when it starts.
- `tick(_context: AIManager) -> int`: Every tick while it runs. The default runs forever.
- `exit(_context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`: Once, when it stops. reason says why, such as "decision", "interrupted", "succeeded", "failed" or "removed".
- `passes_requirements(owned_words: PackedInt64Array) -> bool`: True if it's enabled and its tag requirements pass for the pawn's owned tags, given as words (`OwnedTags.get_words()`).
- `tag_words() -> PackedInt64Array`: Its own `tags` as words, parents included, for score modifiers' applies_to.
- `is_cooling_down(at_tick: int) -> bool`: True while its cooldown (as its modifiers leave it) hasn't finished.
- `effective_jitter() -> float`: This behaviour's jitter amount before modifiers: its own, or the manager's default when it's -1.
- `modified(number: int, base: float) -> float`: One of its numbers as its modifiers leave it: base times their multiplies plus their adds, or the last override.
- `score_bonus() -> float`: What its modifiers add to its score (0 with none).
- `current_jitter() -> float`: Its jitter amount with modifiers, never below 0.
- `current_interrupt_threshold() -> int`: Its interrupt threshold with modifiers.
- `current_cooldown_ticks() -> int`: Its cooldown with modifiers, in this match's ticks; 0: none.
- `current_min_run_ticks() -> int`: Its minimum run with modifiers, in this match's ticks; 0: none.

## AIBehaviourManager

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIBehaviourManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Picks and runs the pawn's AI behaviour, judging between its behaviours by score.

A component of the pawn's AIManager (added by PawnInitializer, or the game's AI brain) with its [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase) nodes as children. At each decision it checks whether the running behaviour may be replaced, drops behaviours that fail a hard rule, scores the rest and starts the winner; between decisions only the running behaviour's tick runs. Behaviours are kept sorted by name (the fixed order), never by the order added. Outside code only talks to the manager:

```gdscript
pawn.ai.behaviour_manager.get_running_behaviour()
pawn.ai.behaviour_manager.add_modifier(charge_shout, self)   # raise melee until removed (AIBehaviourModifier)
pawn.ai.behaviour_manager.remove_modifiers(self)
```

C++ makes the decisions (its own `AIDecider`, through `cpp`) and this manager is the backup (`decide()`). Design: pawn spec 10.7, 10.8 and 16.5, scaling spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `decision_listener: Callable` = `Callable()`: Called after every decision of every pawn: `func(record: AIDecisionRecord, manager: AIBehaviourManager)`. Static, so one listener hears every pawn. For diagnostics and checking another decider (scaling spec 6.2). Empty (default): no record is made.
- `decides_in: int` = `0`: Where this pawn's decisions are made: C++ (the default) or GDScript. The project setting `AIDeciderBridge.ALL_IN_GDSCRIPT_SETTING` and diagnostics ([`AIDecisionChecks`](../diagnostics/REFERENCE.md#aidecisionchecks)) can move every pawn to GDScript.
- `default_score_jitter: float` = `0.0`: The jitter for behaviours whose own score_jitter is -1. 0: no randomness.
- `randomize_ties: bool` = `false`: On: results that tie are picked between at random (replayably). Off: the fixed order decides.
- `tie_margin: float` = `0.0001`: Results closer than this count as a tie.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this is a part of, or null.
- `cpp: AIDeciderBridge` = `null`: Its link to its C++ decider, or null while it decides in GDScript. Made at its first decision, and again when its brain or where it decides changes.
- `modifiers_version: int` = `0`: Goes up by one whenever what the behaviour modifiers do to any behaviour changes, so the C++ decider's copy is written again.

### Signals

- `behaviour_changed(old_behaviour: AIBehaviourBase, new_behaviour: AIBehaviourBase, reason: String)`: Sent each time the running behaviour changes. Either can be null: nothing was running, or nothing runs now.

### Constants

- `DecidesIn.CPP = 0`: by C++, the main path (the default)
- `DecidesIn.GDSCRIPT = 1`: by this manager, the backup
- `TIE_SALT = 28981`
- `MODIFIER_TAG_SOURCE = &"behaviour_modifiers"`

### Functions

- `get_running_behaviour() -> AIBehaviourBase`: The behaviour running now, or null.
- `get_behaviours() -> AIBehaviourBase[]`: Every behaviour, in the fixed order.
- `get_behaviour_list() -> AIBehaviourBase[]`: The same list without a copy, for code that reads it often (the C++ decider's bridge). Don't change it.
- `describe() -> Dictionary`: This brain as plain data: the manager's, the AI context's and each behaviour's settings, in the fixed order. Taken by `AIDecider.add_brain()` and saved by [`AIDecisionRecorder`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_aidecisionrecorder.html). Settings changed during play show in the next call.
- `decide(tick: int, record: AIDecisionRecord = null) -> void`: Makes the waiting decision (`AIManager.request_decision()`) and starts what it chose. record: filled in while `decision_listener` is set (null: made here). Twin of C++ `AIDecider`: same steps, a change goes in both.
- `tick_running(tick: int) -> void`: `AIManager.think()` calls this every tick the AI runs, after any decision. Ticks the running behaviour.
- `stop_running(reason: String) -> void`: Stops the running behaviour, if any; its exit() gets this reason. Called with "died" when the pawn dies.
- `inputs_changed() -> void`: Called when a behaviour's conditions change (`AIBehaviourBase.rebuild_conditions()`), so the inputs worked out at each decision are listed again, and C++ gets the new brain.
- `settings_changed() -> void`: Called when a behaviour's settings change in play (`AIBehaviourBase.use_definition()`): its inputs, the modifiers that count for it (its tags may have changed) and C++'s brain are worked out again.
- `add_modifier(modifier: AIBehaviourModifier, source: Variant) -> void`: Adds a behaviour modifier (pawn spec 16.5), kept under this source: anything that names it, usually the node or effect that adds it. A source may add several; `remove_modifiers()` takes all of its own away.
- `remove_modifiers(source: Variant) -> void`: Takes away every behaviour modifier this source added.
- `get_modifiers() -> Dictionary[]`: The behaviour modifiers now, in the order added: {modifier, source, ends, only} each (ends is the tick it goes, -1 until removed; only is the behaviour that gave it to itself, or null).
- `refresh_modifiers(tick: int) -> void`: Works out again what the modifiers do to each behaviour's numbers and which they block, if anything they depend on changed: the list, a deadline passing, or the pawn's owned tags (their ongoing requirements). Every decision calls it first; cheap when nothing changed.
- `check_running(tick: int) -> void`: The AI step calls this every run, before deciding: if the owned tags or the modifiers changed and the running behaviour's tag requirements now fail (or a modifier blocks it), it asks for a decision that its min_run_ticks don't hold off (its interrupt_threshold still does). A pawn out of shots leaves Keep Distance at once instead of at its next decision tick.
- `worked_out_inputs() -> PackedInt32Array`: The slots of the worked-out inputs any behaviour's conditions or curves read, listed once (and again after inputs_changed()).

## AIBehaviourModifier

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIBehaviourModifier.gd`, extends [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition)

A change to some behaviours while it lasts: "Charge!" raising melee, fear lowering fighting, confusion's extra jitter, a block.

The generic modifier (pawn spec 16.5, 16.9) aimed at behaviours by their tags: it changes one of their numbers (`number`), multiplying, then adding, or overriding it (the last added wins). A designer-made [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition) (with variants), given to a pawn's behaviour manager by whatever causes it and kept under that source:

```gdscript
pawn.ai.behaviour_manager.add_modifier(charge_shout, self)
pawn.ai.behaviour_manager.remove_modifiers(self)
```

A behaviour can also apply one to itself as it starts or ends (`AIBehaviourDefinition.modifier_on_start`). The C++ decider gets the numbers they leave, not the modifiers. Only on the server, where the AI runs.

### Settings and properties

- `applies_to: TagQuery`: Which behaviours it changes: a query over each behaviour's own tags (`AIBehaviourDefinition.tags`), such as any of ai.stance.melee. Empty: every behaviour, or, given by a behaviour to itself as it starts or ends, only that behaviour.
- `number: int` = `0`: Which number it changes.
- `multiply: float` = `1.0`: The number is multiplied by this, before the adds. 1: nothing. Multiplies from several modifiers combine.
- `add: float` = `0.0`: Added after the multiplies. Negative takes away. A score bonus of -0.3 drops a behaviour that scores 0.6 to 0.3.
- `overrides: bool` = `false`: On: the number takes `override_value`, whatever the others do (the last one added wins). A berserk state's threshold.
- `override_value: float` = `0.0`: With `overrides`, the number's value.
- `blocks: bool` = `false`: On: the behaviours it applies to can't be chosen while it counts, and a running one is replaced; its number change is ignored.
- `duration_ticks: int` = `0`: How long it lasts once added, in ticks at 60 a second; the manager keeps the tick it ends. 0: until its source removes it.
- `ongoing_requirements: TagQuery`: It counts only while the pawn's owned tags pass this, such as none of status.has_ammo. Empty: always.
- `granted_tags: StringName[]` = `[]`: Tags the pawn owns while it's added, so other queries can see it (an "ai.stance.melee" order, say).
- `wakes_decision: bool` = `false`: On: adding or removing it asks for a decision at once. Off by default: hundreds of pawns deciding on one tick is a spike.

### Constants

- `Number.SCORE_BONUS = 0`: added to its score, in the units of max_score (0 with no modifier)
- `Number.SCORE_JITTER = 1`: the ± random offset on its score (AIBehaviourDefinition.score_jitter, or the manager's default)
- `Number.INTERRUPT_THRESHOLD = 2`: how strong an event must be to replace it while it runs
- `Number.COOLDOWN_TICKS = 3`: ticks after it ends before it can be chosen again, at 60 a second
- `Number.MIN_RUN_TICKS = 4`: ticks an ordinary decision can't replace it once chosen, at 60 a second

### Functions

- `applies_to_behaviour(behaviour: AIBehaviourBase, only: AIBehaviourBase = null) -> bool`: True if it applies to this behaviour. only: the behaviour that gave it to itself (null: none), which an empty applies_to means.
- `counts_for(owned_words: PackedInt64Array) -> bool`: True if it counts for owned tags given as words (its ongoing requirements pass).

## AIDeciderBridge

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIDeciderBridge.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Links one pawn's [`AIBehaviourManager`](#aibehaviourmanager) to its C++ decider (`AIDecider`, the main path): keeps the decider's row up to date and asks it for each decision.

The manager makes one (`make_for()`) when the pawn decides in C++, and drops it when it moves to GDScript. Before each decision it reads the version counters of the facts the row holds and copies only what changed: the owned tags (the AI's state among them), the behaviour modifiers' numbers, the actions that could start, the AI's facts (`AIManager.facts_version`: target, last hit, the swing coming) and a game's inputs (`AIInputs.kept_version`). A behaviour C++ can't judge from data (`AIBehaviourBase.judged_in_gdscript()`) gets GDScript's answers, written in before each decision; C++ judges the rest. Brains are compiled once per behaviour set and shared by every decider. Where pawns decide: `AIBehaviourManager.decides_in`, the project setting `ALL_IN_GDSCRIPT_SETTING`, and diagnostics' switches ([`AIDecisionChecks`](../diagnostics/REFERENCE.md#aidecisionchecks)). Timed as `ai.decide.cpp`. Design: pawn spec 16.5, scaling spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `decisions: int` = `0`: The decisions made in C++ so far, by every pawn.
- `gdscript_answers: int` = `0`: The answers GDScript gave so far for behaviours C++ can't judge (code of their own, or a condition C++ doesn't read).
- `decider: Object` = `null`: The C++ AIDecider, holding this pawn's row. Typed Object so the game runs without the library.
- `manager: AIBehaviourManager` = `null`: The behaviour manager it decides for.

### Constants

- `ALL_IN_GDSCRIPT_SETTING = "project_base/ai/all_decisions_in_gdscript"`: The project setting that has every pawn decide in GDScript, the backup (false: each pawn's own decides_in).

### Functions

- `make_for(for_manager: AIBehaviourManager) -> AIDeciderBridge` *(static)*: A bridge for this manager, or null if it decides in GDScript.
- `placement_version() -> int` *(static)*: Where pawns decide changes when this does: diagnostics' switches, the tags the brains' masks were made with. A manager places itself again when it differs from what it last saw.
- `placement_changed() -> void` *(static)*: Every pawn settles where it decides again at its next decision.
- `decide(tick: int, event_priority: int, event_normal: bool) -> int`: One decision in C++: copies over the facts that changed, asks the decider, and returns the chosen behaviour's slot (-1 nothing). C++ applies the switch to its own copy of the state; the manager starts the behaviour.
- `was_kept() -> bool`: Whether the interrupt rule kept the running behaviour at the last decision.
- `copy_state() -> void`: Copies the decision state from the behaviour nodes (running behaviour, its start, each one's last end) over C++'s: as it starts, and after shadow mode finds a disagreement.
- `stopped(tick: int) -> void`: The running behaviour stopped without a decision (finished, died, removed): C++'s copy of the state follows.
- `written_facts() -> Dictionary`: The facts as written into the row (owned, target_id, can_press and the modifiers' numbers), for the checks.
- `last_inputs() -> PackedFloat64Array`: The inputs the last decision used, as C++ worked them out, for the checks.
- `can_press_mask(for_manager: AIBehaviourManager) -> int` *(static)*: The behaviours whose action could start now, as a mask by behaviour slot.

## AIDecisionRecord

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIDecisionRecord.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

What one AI decision was made from, and what it chose: a plain record for diagnostics and for checking another decider.

The [`AIBehaviourManager`](#aibehaviourmanager) fills one in after each decision, only while `AIBehaviourManager.decision_listener` is set; the [`AIDecisionRecorder`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_aidecisionrecorder.html) keeps and saves them. It holds the reasons, the situation, each behaviour's hard rule, range, availability and score in the fixed order, and the choice. Behaviours the early stop skipped show `available = -1`. Nothing in the game reads records.

```gdscript
record.chosen                              # &"Chase", or &"" for nothing
record.behaviours[0]["name"]               # each entry is a Dictionary, see add_behaviour()
record.to_dict()                           # everything as plain values, for saving as JSON
```

Design: scaling spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `tick: int` = `0`: The tick of the decision.
- `pawn_number: int` = `0`: The pawn's own number (`AIManager.pawn_number()`), which also goes into its random numbers.
- `pawn_name: StringName` = `&""`: The pawn's node name, for reading.
- `cause: StringName` = `&"direct"`: Why it decided: one of the CAUSE_ constants.
- `event_priority: int` = `0`: The strongest reason's priority (pawn spec 10.7).
- `event_is_normal: bool` = `true`: True when every reason was an ordinary decision tick, the one kind min_run_ticks holds off.
- `target_before_id: int` = `0`: The target before and after the target selector's update, as instance ids (0: none) and names. Only for `CAUSE_AI_STEP`; otherwise both are what it was.
- `target_before_name: StringName` = `&""`
- `target_after_id: int` = `0`
- `target_after_name: StringName` = `&""`
- `state_before: StringName` = `&""`: The state before and after the state manager's update. Only for `CAUSE_AI_STEP`.
- `state_after: StringName` = `&""`
- `state: StringName` = `&""`: The state the behaviours were judged in.
- `owned_tags: StringName[]` = `[]`: The tags the pawn owned when the behaviours were judged (without their parents), sorted.
- `has_target: bool` = `false`: True if there was a target when the behaviours were judged.
- `running_before: StringName` = `&""`: The behaviour running before the decision (&"": none), and the tick it started (-1: none).
- `running_started_tick: int` = `-1`
- `kept_by_interrupt: bool` = `false`: True when the running behaviour couldn't be replaced for this reason (step 0), so no behaviour was looked at.
- `behaviours: Dictionary[]` = `[]`: One Dictionary per behaviour, in the manager's fixed order; only the running one's (`RULE_KEPT`) when `kept_by_interrupt`. See `add_behaviour()`.
- `inputs: PackedFloat64Array` = `PackedFloat64Array()`: The pawn's AI inputs as this decision worked them out (`AIInputs.values`), by slot: what the behaviours' conditions read.
- `chosen: StringName` = `&""`: What runs after the decision: a behaviour's name, or &"" for nothing.

### Constants

- `CAUSE_AI_STEP = &"ai_step"`: Why the decision happened: the pawn's AI step (a decision tick, or an event such as a hit or a state change).
- `CAUSE_BEHAVIOUR_ENDED = &"behaviour_ended"`: Why: the running behaviour finished (SUCCEEDED or FAILED), which decides at once, with no target or state update first.
- `CAUSE_DIRECT = &"direct"`: Why: something called `AIBehaviourManager.decide()` itself, such as a test.
- `RULE_NONE = &""`: A hard rule that ruled a behaviour out before any of its own code ran (pawn spec 10.8 step 2). None: it was a candidate.
- `RULE_TAGS = &"tags"`: Its tag requirements failed for the pawn's owned tags (the AI's state is one of them).
- `RULE_OFF = &"off"`: Switched off (`AIBehaviourBase.enabled`).
- `RULE_BLOCKED = &"blocked"`: A behaviour modifier blocks it.
- `RULE_COOLDOWN = &"cooldown"`: Cooling down.
- `RULE_NO_TARGET = &"no_target"`: Needs a target, and there's none.
- `RULE_ACTION = &"action"`: Its action couldn't start (AbilityManager.can_start).
- `RULE_NOT_WORKED_OUT = &"cpp"`: Passed the hard rules, but C++ made the decision, so GDScript's range, availability and score weren't worked out.
- `RULE_KEPT = &"kept"`: The running behaviour the interrupt rule kept: only its numbers, which the rule read (its threshold and minimum run).

### Functions

- `note_target_before(target: Node3D) -> void`: Notes the target before the selector's update.
- `note_target_after(target: Node3D) -> void`: Notes the target after the selector's update.
- `changed() -> bool`: True when the running behaviour changed.
- `add_behaviour(behaviour: AIBehaviourBase, rule: StringName) -> void`: One behaviour's entry, from the manager's scratch values; rule: what ruled it out, or `RULE_NONE`. Keys: name, rule, and its numbers with modifiers (modifier: the score bonus, jitter_amount, interrupt_threshold, min_run at the match's rate); a candidate's also jitter (this decision's offset), ceiling, floor (null: none), available (1, 0, -1 never asked) and score (null: not scored).
- `entry_for(behaviour_name: StringName) -> Dictionary`: The entry for this behaviour, or an empty Dictionary.
- `to_dict() -> Dictionary`: Everything as plain values (text, numbers, arrays, dictionaries), ready for JSON.

## AIInputs

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIInputs.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

One pawn's AI inputs: the named numbers its behaviours' conditions read.

Every name has a slot, the same for every pawn, so a crowd's inputs line up as one table the C++ decider reads. The built-in inputs (the constants below) are worked out the first time a condition reads them in a decision; any other name is a game's own, kept until written again (`set_input()`). Names starting `ticks_` are times in ticks, written for 60 a second. Design: scaling spec 6.2.

```gdscript
pawn.ai.inputs.set_input(&"morale", 0.4)
pawn.ai.inputs.value_of(AIInputs.TARGET_DISTANCE)
```

### Settings and properties

- `values: PackedFloat64Array` = `PackedFloat64Array()`: The values by slot; 0 where nothing was written or worked out.
- `kept_version: int` = `0`: Goes up by one whenever a kept input (a game's own) is written, so the C++ decider copies them again ([`AIDeciderBridge`](#aideciderbridge)).

### Constants

- `TARGET_DISTANCE = &"target_distance"`: Flat distance to where the AI last knew its target to be; `FAR` with no target.
- `MOST_AWARE_CERTAIN = &"most_aware_certain"`: 1 if the memory entry it's most aware of is certain, else 0.
- `MOST_AWARE_UNCERTAIN = &"most_aware_uncertain"`: 1 if there's a most aware entry and it isn't certain yet, else 0.
- `TICKS_SINCE_UNKNOWN_HIT = &"ticks_since_unknown_hit"`: Ticks since an attacker it doesn't remember hit it; `FAR` if none did, or the attacker is remembered.
- `INCOMING_ATTACK = &"incoming_attack"`: 1 while a swing it was warned of hasn't hit yet.
- `INCOMING_ATTACK_TICK = &"incoming_attack_tick"`: The tick that swing started.
- `INCOMING_ATTACKER = &"incoming_attacker"`: The swinging pawn's number.
- `GROUP_DISTANCE = "group_distance/"`: `group_distance/<group>`: flat distance to the group's nearest node; `FAR` if it has none.
- `GROUP_FOUND = "group_found/"`: `group_found/<group>`: 1 while the group has a node. Pair it with a "further than" check on the distance.
- `ACTION_READY = "action_ready/"`: `action_ready/<action>`: 1 while pressing the action could start an ability.
- `TICKS_PREFIX = "ticks_"`: Names starting with this are times in ticks.
- `FAR = 1000000000000.0`: The value when there's nothing to measure: larger than any real distance or time, and not INF, so records stay valid JSON.
- `Kind.KEPT = 0`
- `Kind.TARGET_DISTANCE = 1`
- `Kind.MOST_AWARE_CERTAIN = 2`
- `Kind.MOST_AWARE_UNCERTAIN = 3`
- `Kind.TICKS_SINCE_UNKNOWN_HIT = 4`
- `Kind.INCOMING_ATTACK = 5`
- `Kind.INCOMING_ATTACK_TICK = 6`
- `Kind.INCOMING_ATTACKER = 7`
- `Kind.GROUP_DISTANCE = 8`
- `Kind.GROUP_FOUND = 9`
- `Kind.ACTION_READY = 10`
- `GROUP_LOOK_AGAIN_TICKS = 120`: How often a group's nearest node is looked for again, in ticks at 60 a second.

### Functions

- `slot_of(input_name: StringName) -> int` *(static)*: The slot for an input name, given out on first use.
- `input_count() -> int` *(static)*: How many names have slots.
- `name_of(slot: int) -> StringName` *(static)*: The name in a slot.
- `is_worked_out(slot: int) -> bool` *(static)*: True for a built-in input, worked out at each decision.
- `kind_of(slot: int) -> int` *(static)*: A slot's `Kind`.
- `parameter_of(slot: int) -> StringName` *(static)*: The name after a slot's prefix (the group or action); &"" for others.
- `kinds() -> PackedInt32Array` *(static)*: Every slot's `Kind`, for the C++ decider.
- `is_ticks(slot: int) -> bool` *(static)*: True if the slot's input is a time in ticks.
- `half_noticed_conditions(hit_memory_ticks: int) -> AICondition[]` *(static)*: The conditions for "something half-noticed", shared by Look Toward and Investigate: the most aware entry isn't certain yet, or an unknown attacker hit within hit_memory_ticks.
- `set_input(input_name: StringName, amount: float) -> void`: Writes a game's own input; it stays until written again.
- `set_slot(slot: int, amount: float) -> void`: Writes a value by slot. Writing a kept input raises `kept_version`.
- `value(slot: int) -> float`: The value in a slot, working out a built-in one if it hasn't been yet this decision.
- `value_of(input_name: StringName) -> float`: The value of an input by name.
- `begin_decision(tick: int) -> void`: Starts a decision: built-in inputs are worked out again when next read.
- `fill(slots: PackedInt32Array) -> void`: Works out every listed slot now, for something that needs them all (a decision record, shadow mode).
- `nearest_in_group(group: StringName, tick: int) -> Node3D`: The group's nearest node (null if none), kept for 2 seconds while it exists. Go To Point walks to it.
- `action_ready(action: StringName) -> bool`: True if pressing the action could start an ability. Asks the AbilityManager again only after its readiness_version moved on, or every time for an action whose readiness follows the body (Jump).

## AIManager

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The pawn's AI: holds its AI components as children, what they share, and the step that runs them in order.

A component on the pawn (`Pawn.ai`), added by PawnInitializer from parts/AIManager.tscn. Its children are the AI's components: the [`AIController`](../controllers/REFERENCE.md#aicontroller) (the AI's hands), [`AISensingManager`](#aisensingmanager), [`AIMemory`](#aimemory), [`AITargetSelector`](#aitargetselector), [`AIStateManager`](#aistatemanager) and [`AIBehaviourManager`](#aibehaviourmanager). A pawn scene overrides one by putting its own of that name under its AIManager; PawnInitializer fills in the rest. It makes no decisions: it holds what the components share (the pawn, the current target, the pawn's [`AIInputs`](#aiinputs), the last hit and swing coming, the waiting decision, and random numbers that replay the same), and the pawn calls `run_ai()` from its own tick, which runs `think()`. Behaviours and states get it as their "context" (`context.memory`, `context.current_tick`, `context.random_unit(salt)`). Code outside the AI asks through its request inbox (`add_modifier()`, `remove_modifiers()`, `set_input()`): requests wait for the pawn's next AI step and apply in the order asked, so no result depends on which pawn ran first. Design: pawn spec 10, 10.7, 10.9 and 16.5.

### Settings and properties

- `while_possessed: int` = `1`: What the AI does while a player has the pawn. MEMORY_ONLY suits possessing an NPC and letting go: the AI already knows what's around.
- `decision_interval_ticks: int` = `15`: How often the AI decides, in ticks at 60 a second (15: four times a second). Each pawn is offset by its own number, so a crowd doesn't all decide on one tick. Some events wake a decision early (pawn spec 10.9).
- `random_seed: int` = `0`: Part of every random number this AI uses, with the match seed; entity numbers still make two pawns differ.
- `order_source: Callable` = `Callable()`: Where every AI pawn's orders come from, if not from its own AI: called instead of `think()` in each pawn's AI step, as `order_source.call(context, tick)`, to tell `context.controller` what to do. Empty (the default): the AI thinks. For playing back an order stream (netcode spec 19.3), recorded through `AIController.order_listener`.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this AI belongs to, or null if its parent isn't one.
- `current_tick: int` = `0`: The tick the AI is running now. Set by `run_ai()` at the start of each AI step.
- `current_target: Node3D` = `null`: What the AI is focused on, picked by the target selector. Null when there's none.
- `facts_version: int` = `0`: Goes up by one whenever a fact the C++ decider works inputs out from changes: the target, the last hit, the swing coming at it ([`AIDeciderBridge`](#aideciderbridge) copies them again before the next decision).
- `inputs: AIInputs` = `null`: The pawn's AI inputs, the numbers its behaviours' conditions read ([`AIInputs`](#aiinputs)). Worked out at each decision; a game writes its own with `inputs.set_input(name, value)`.
- `controller: AIController`: The AI's hands, or null if it has no AIController. The pawn's ControllerManager puts it in charge while no player has the pawn.
- `state_manager: AIStateManager`: The pawn's state manager, or null.
- `behaviour_manager: AIBehaviourManager`: The pawn's behaviour manager, or null.
- `sensing_manager: AISensingManager`: The pawn's sensing manager, or null.
- `memory: AIMemory`: The pawn's memory, or null.
- `target_selector: AITargetSelector`: The pawn's target selector, or null.
- `last_hit_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick of the last hit this pawn took, noted from the AbilityManager's hit_arrived on the server; -1: never hit. Not a memory entry: there's no damage sense.
- `last_attacker: Node3D` = `null`: Who made the last hit.
- `last_hit_from: Vector3` = `Vector3(0, 0, 0)`: Where the attacker stood when it hit.
- `incoming_attacker: Pawn` = `null`: Who swung the latest swing coming at this pawn (`note_incoming_attack()`), for AIParryBehaviour, or null.
- `incoming_start_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick that swing started.
- `incoming_hit_tick: int` = `-1`: The tick that swing's hit starts; -1 when nothing is coming.

### Constants

- `WhilePossessed.OFF = 0`: nothing runs
- `WhilePossessed.MEMORY_ONLY = 1`: sensing and memory run; states and behaviours pause. The default
- `WhilePossessed.FULL = 2`: everything runs. The AI controller keeps its last order without acting on it until it's in charge again

### Functions

- `current_target_index() -> int`: The memory index of the current target, or -1.
- `most_aware_index() -> int`: The memory index of the entry with the highest awareness now, or -1.
- `refresh_shared_inputs() -> void`: Clears the shared inputs, so the next read works them out again. Setting current_target does it.
- `current_state_name() -> StringName`: The name of the current state, such as &"Idle", or &"" before the first state is picked.
- `note_hit(hit: HitInfo) -> void`: Called for the AbilityManager's hit_arrived. Notes the hit and asks for a decision at once, so the pawn reacts this tick.
- `note_incoming_attack(attacker: Pawn, start_tick: int, hit_tick: int) -> void`: Called by an enemy's MeleeAttackAbility or FireProjectileStep, on the server, when it starts an attack that may reach this pawn. Notes it and asks for a decision at once, since a swing's windup is shorter than the time between ordinary decisions.
- `has_incoming_attack() -> bool`: True while a noted swing hasn't hit yet and its attacker is still there and alive.
- `clear_incoming_attack() -> void`: Forgets the noted swing, once it's been answered.
- `was_hit_within(ticks: int) -> bool`: True if the pawn was hit within this many ticks, counted at 60 a second like every AI setting (converted to the match's rate).
- `last_attacker_is_known() -> bool`: True if the last attacker is in memory.
- `unknown_hit_point(within_ticks: int) -> Variant`: Where an unknown attacker hit from, if that was within this many ticks; null otherwise. Look Toward and Investigate head there when nothing else is half-noticed.
- `point_of_interest(within_ticks: int) -> Variant`: Something half-noticed to look at or go and see: the most aware memory entry's last known position while it isn't certain yet, or else where an unremembered attacker hit from, within this many ticks (at 60 a second); null when neither. Their conditions check the same facts through `AIInputs.half_noticed_conditions()`, which the C++ decider can read.
- `has_target() -> bool`: True when there's a current target, picked by the target selector.
- `run_ai(tick: int) -> void`: The AI's step, called by the pawn in its input phase. Runs only where the AI runs (offline or the server), never while a rollback replays ticks. The pawn's orders for the tick come from `order_source` if one is set, else from `think()`.
- `think(tick: int) -> void`: The AI thinking, in a fixed order (pawn spec 4, 10.9 and 16.5): the request inbox, sensing, a decision when one is due, the running behaviour. While a player has the pawn, only as far as `while_possessed` allows. `run_ai()` calls it; an `order_source` may too.
- `add_modifier(modifier: AIBehaviourModifier, source: Variant) -> void`: Asks for a behaviour modifier to be added under this source (`AIBehaviourManager.add_modifier()`), at the pawn's next AI step.
- `remove_modifiers(source: Variant) -> void`: Asks for every behaviour modifier this source added to be taken away, at the pawn's next AI step.
- `set_input(input_name: StringName, value: float) -> void`: Asks for one of the AI's own inputs (a game's, such as &"morale") to be set, at the pawn's next AI step (`AIInputs.set_input()`).
- `apply_requests() -> void`: Applies the requests waiting in the inbox, in the order asked. `think()` calls it first; a test can call it directly.
- `waiting_requests() -> int`: How many requests are waiting for the pawn's next AI step.
- `is_decision_tick(tick: int) -> bool`: True on this pawn's regular decision ticks, every `decision_interval_ticks`, offset by its own number.
- `request_decision(priority: int = 0, normal: bool = true) -> void`: Asks for a decision this tick. priority is how strong the reason is: 0 for an ordinary decision, a state's priority for a state change. normal is true only for an ordinary decision, the one kind a behaviour's min_run_ticks holds off. Several requests in one tick combine into one decision with the strongest reason.
- `has_decision_waiting() -> bool`: True when a decision is waiting to happen.
- `waiting_event_priority() -> int`: The strongest reason for the waiting decision. Only meaningful while one is waiting.
- `waiting_event_is_normal() -> bool`: True when the waiting decision is only an ordinary one.
- `clear_decision() -> void`: The behaviour manager calls this once it has made the decision.
- `random_unit(salt: int) -> float`: A number from 0 up to (not including) 1 for this tick. salt says what it's for (a behaviour uses its name's hash). The same seed, pawn, tick and salt give the same number on every machine and run.
- `random_unit_at(tick: int, salt: int) -> float`: random_unit() for a given tick.
- `random_signed(salt: int) -> float`: A number from -1 to 1. See random_unit().
- `effective_seed() -> int`: The seed this AI's rolls use: `random_seed` plus the match's (`DeterministicRandom.match_seed`). The C++ decider is given the same when the pawn joins it.

## AIMemory

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIMemory.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

What a pawn's AI has sensed, and how aware of each thing it is: awareness that rises when seen and fades when not.

A component of the pawn's AIManager. One entry per sensed entity: its last known position, when it was last seen, its awareness (0 to 1), whether it's certain, and its threat. The entries live in a store, `AIMemoryStore` in the navcore C++ library or else [`AIMemoryStoreGD`](#aimemorystoregd) (same rules); this node keeps the settings and signals and passes calls on. It asks for a decision when an entity is first sensed or becomes certain. Indexes stay valid until the next `forget_old()`, so use them within one tick:

```gdscript
var i := pawn.ai.memory.find(entity)   # -1 when it isn't remembered
pawn.ai.memory.awareness_at(i, tick)
pawn.ai.memory.is_certain_at(i)
pawn.ai.memory.add_threat(entity, 5.0)
```

Design: pawn spec 10.5 and 10.11.

### Settings and properties

- `uncertain_fade_delay_ticks: int` = `300`: Ticks (at 60 a second) an uncertain entry stays at full awareness after it was last seen, before its fade starts. 300 is 5 s, so a glimpse that reached Alert keeps the pawn Alert long enough to look and walk over.
- `uncertain_fade: FadeProfile`: How awareness fades for uncertain entries after the delay. Empty: a straight line to nothing over 300 ticks.
- `certain_fade_delay_ticks: int` = `0`: The same delay for certain entries. Longer keeps a pawn searching longer after losing sight of an enemy.
- `certain_fade: FadeProfile`: How awareness fades for certain entries after the delay. Empty: a straight line to nothing over 1200 ticks (20 s).
- `continuous_sighting_ticks: int` = `30`: Two sightings no more than this many ticks apart, with no unseen check between, count as one continuous look, so awareness doesn't fade between them. Keep it at least as long as the senses' gap between checks.
- `threat_per_damage: float` = `0.01`: Threat added to an attacker's entry per health point of damage it does to this pawn (the StatusManager adds it); target selection weighs threat.
- `use_native: bool` = `true`: Off, every AIMemory made from now on uses the GDScript store, even with the C++ library. For tests comparing the two. Read once, when each memory is made.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this is a part of, or null.

### Signals

- `entity_became_certain(entity: Node3D)`: Sent when an entry first reaches full awareness.
- `entity_forgotten(entity: Node3D)`: Sent when an entry is forgotten.

### Functions

- `is_native() -> bool`: True when the C++ store runs.
- `get_store() -> Object`: The store itself, for SightSense and AITargetSelector, which hand it whole loops.
- `entry_count() -> int`: How many entries there are.
- `find(entity: Object) -> int`: The entry for this entity, or -1.
- `entity_at(index: int) -> Node3D`: The entity of an entry, or null if it's been freed.
- `awareness_at(index: int, tick: int) -> float`: Awareness of an entry at this tick, faded since it was last seen.
- `is_certain_at(index: int) -> bool`: True if the entry has reached full awareness since it was first sensed.
- `last_known_position_at(index: int) -> Vector3`: Where the entry's entity was last seen.
- `ticks_since_seen_at(index: int, tick: int) -> int`: Ticks since the entry's entity was last seen.
- `threat_at(index: int) -> float`: The entry's threat (see `add_threat()`).
- `ticks_since_checked(entity: Object, tick: int, fallback: int) -> int`: Ticks since a sense last checked this entity, or fallback if it isn't remembered.
- `record_sighting(entity: Node3D, gain: float, tick: int, position: Vector3) -> void`: A sense saw this entity at this tick. gain is added to its awareness; a certain entry refills to 1.
- `record_check(entity: Object, tick: int) -> void`: A sense checked this entity at this tick and didn't see it.
- `add_threat(entity: Object, amount: float) -> void`: Adds threat to an entity's entry, if it's remembered; threat never goes below 0. Game mechanics call this, such as damage dealt.
- `forget_old(tick: int) -> void`: Forgets entries whose fade has ended or whose entity is gone. The sensing manager calls this on each full pass.
- `most_aware_index(tick: int) -> int`: The entry with the highest awareness now, or -1. Ties go to the nearer last known position, then the lower id.
- `native_store() -> Object`: The C++ memory store (AIMemoryStore), or null when the GDScript one runs. The C++ decider reads it directly for the pawn's inputs.
- `clear() -> void`: Forgets everything.
- `announce_sight_results(results: Array) -> void`: SightSense calls this after a sight check: wakes a decision for a new entry, and sends entity_became_certain.

## AIMemoryStoreGD

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIMemoryStoreGD.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

One pawn's AI memory in GDScript, plus the loops that read and write it: the sight check, the most aware entry, target scoring.

Twin of `AIMemoryStore` in the navcore C++ library: same functions, same rules, used where that library isn't available or `AIMemory.use_native` is off. A change to one goes in the other; ai_perception_selftest expects the same results from each (on this one with `-- --gdscript-store`). [`AIMemory`](#aimemory) owns one and passes the settings in; other code goes through [`AIMemory`](#aimemory), not this. Design: pawn spec 10.4, 10.5 and 10.11.

### Functions

- `configure_fades(uncertain: FadeProfile, uncertain_delay: int, _uncertain_custom: bool, certain: FadeProfile, certain_delay: int, _certain_custom: bool, continuous_sighting_ticks: int) -> void`: The fades and their delays. custom isn't needed here: a profile's own value_at() is always called.
- `entry_count() -> int`
- `find(entity: Object) -> int`
- `entity_at(index: int) -> Object`
- `awareness_at(index: int, tick: int) -> float`
- `is_certain_at(index: int) -> bool`
- `last_known_position_at(index: int) -> Vector3`
- `ticks_since_seen_at(index: int, tick: int) -> int`
- `threat_at(index: int) -> float`
- `ticks_since_checked(entity: Object, tick: int, fallback: int) -> int`
- `record_sighting(entity: Object, gain: float, tick: int, position: Vector3) -> int`: Returns bits: 1 when a new entry was made, 2 when the entry became certain.
- `record_check(entity: Object, tick: int) -> void`
- `add_threat(entity: Object, amount: float) -> void`
- `forget_old(tick: int) -> PackedInt64Array`: Forgets entries whose fade has ended or whose entity is gone or dead. Returns the ids of forgotten entities that still exist.
- `most_aware_index(from: Vector3, tick: int) -> int`: The entry with the highest awareness now, or -1. Ties go to the nearer last known position, then the lower id.
- `clear() -> void`
- `best_target(from: Vector3, awareness_weight: float, distance_weight: float, threat_weight: float, distance_range: float, min_awareness: float, current_id: int, current_bonus: float, tick: int) -> int`: AITargetSelector's formula over every entry. Returns the winning index, or -1.
- `set_sight_settings(settings: PackedFloat64Array) -> void`: SightSense's settings: fill_rate, near_range, sight_range, cos of half the central cone, cos of half the periphery, periphery_multiplier, max_gain_ticks, eye_height, target_height, sight_blocking_mask, sense_interval_ticks.
- `sight_check(observer: Node3D, eye_yaw: float, candidates: Array, tick: int) -> Array`: Checks each candidate from observer's eyes, facing eye_yaw, and records what's seen. Returns [a new entry was made, entities that became certain]. See SightSense for the rules.

## AISenseBase

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AISenseBase.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The base for one AI sense, such as sight: notices other pawns and writes what it found into memory.

A child of the pawn's [`AISensingManager`](#aisensingmanager). A sense never decides anything: it writes into the pawn's [`AIMemory`](#aimemory), with a gain saying how strongly it noticed. Extend it and override `get_range()` (how far it reaches, so the manager's one shared query covers every sense), `full_pass()` (candidates are the other-team pawns in range) and `refresh()` (a cheap check of the current target between full passes). Only [`SightSense`](#sightsense) exists; hearing is deferred. Design: pawn spec 10.4 and 14.

### Settings and properties

- `manager: AISensingManager` = `null`: Set by the AISensingManager.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this sense belongs to. Set by the AISensingManager.
- `perf_full_name: StringName` = `&""`: The timing scope names for its full passes and its refreshes, such as &"ai.sense.Sight.full" and &"ai.sense.Sight.refresh" (see [`PerfScopes`](../diagnostics/REFERENCE.md#perfscopes)). Made once by the manager.
- `perf_refresh_name: StringName` = `&""`

### Functions

- `get_range() -> float`: How far this sense reaches, in metres.
- `full_pass(_candidates: Pawn[], _tick: int) -> void`: On each full pass. candidates are other-team pawns within the manager's query range.
- `refresh(_tick: int) -> void`: Between full passes, for the current target.

## AISensingManager

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AISensingManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Runs a pawn's AI senses on their turn, and finds the other-team pawns they may notice.

A component of the pawn's AIManager with its [`AISenseBase`](#aisensebase) nodes as children (SightSense by default). Every `sense_interval_ticks` a full pass finds the other-team pawns within the longest sense's range, hands them to each sense, then has memory forget faded entries; every `refresh_interval_ticks` in between, each sense refreshes the current target. Both are offset by the pawn's own number. With the navcore C++ library, a full pass's search, visibility and line of sight run on worker threads as a shared sensing job (`AISensingJob`) between ticks; its answers match the main thread's, except for anything that moves a pawn between ticks. Design: pawn spec 10.4 and 8.21, scaling spec steps 1, 2 and 4.

### Settings and properties

- `sense_interval_ticks: int` = `10`: Ticks (at 60 a second) between full passes: 10 is six a second.
- `refresh_interval_ticks: int` = `5`: Ticks between cheap refreshes of what's already in memory.
- `candidate_mask: int` = `2`: Physics layers the shared query looks on. Pawns are on layer 2.
- `max_candidates: int` = `32`: The most pawns one query returns.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this is a part of, or null.

### Functions

- `get_senses() -> AISenseBase[]`: Every sense, in tree order.
- `tick_sensing(tick: int) -> void`: `AIManager.think()` calls this each tick the pawn's AI runs.
- `full_pass(tick: int) -> void`: One full pass now. `tick_sensing()` calls it on schedule; tests may call it directly.
- `get_range() -> float`: The longest range among the senses, in metres.

## AIStateBase

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIStateBase.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The base for one AI state, such as Idle, Alert or Combat: "what situation am I in".

A child of the pawn's [`AIStateManager`](#aistatemanager). A state doesn't act: it decides which behaviours are allowed (they list states by node name) and, with its `priority`, how strong a reason its arrival is for interrupting the running behaviour. The manager checks each state's `prerequisites_met()` from the highest priority down and the first that holds wins; there is no minimum time in a state. Extend it and override `prerequisites_met()`, reading thresholds from exports so designers can tune them; optionally `enter()` and `exit()`. Its node name is its name. Design: pawn spec 10.6.

### Settings and properties

- `priority: int` = `0`: Higher is checked first. A state change is also an interrupt event of this priority (pawn spec 10.7).
- `tag: StringName` = `&""`: The tag the pawn owns while in this state (tag spec 3), on the server. Empty: ai.state.<its node name in snake case>, such as ai.state.combat. Declare it in the tag declarations.
- `manager: AIStateManager` = `null`: Set by the AIStateManager.
- `perf_name: StringName` = `&""`: The timing scope name for its prerequisites_met(), such as &"ai.state.Combat" (see [`PerfScopes`](../diagnostics/REFERENCE.md#perfscopes)). Made once by the manager.

### Functions

- `get_tag() -> StringName`: The tag the pawn owns while in this state: `tag`, or ai.state.<its node name in snake case>.
- `prerequisites_met(_context: AIManager) -> bool`: Whether this state fits right now. The base never fits, so a state that forgets to override this is never picked by mistake.
- `enter(_context: AIManager) -> void`: Once, when the pawn enters this state.
- `exit(_context: AIManager) -> void`: Once, when the pawn leaves this state.

## AIStateManager

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AIStateManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Picks the pawn's current AI state: the highest-priority state whose prerequisites hold.

A component of the pawn's AIManager with its [`AIStateBase`](#aistatebase) nodes as children. At each decision it moves the pawn to the first state, checked from the highest priority down, whose prerequisites hold, and a change asks for a decision with the new state's priority as the reason. States are sorted by priority, then name, once, when the manager is ready. Server and offline only. The pawn owns the current state's tag (`AIStateBase.get_tag()`, such as ai.state.combat) in its [`OwnedTags`](../tags/REFERENCE.md#ownedtags), so behaviours gate on it. There's no forcing: a scripted state is a state whose prerequisites read a tag the script grants (pawn spec 16.5).

```gdscript
pawn.ai.state_manager.get_current_state()   # an AIStateBase, or null before the first pick
```

Design: pawn spec 10.6, 16.5.

### Settings and properties

- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this is a part of, or null.

### Signals

- `state_changed(old_state: AIStateBase, new_state: AIStateBase, reason: String)`: Sent once each time the state changes. old_state is null for the first pick.

### Functions

- `get_current_state() -> AIStateBase`: The current state, or null before the first pick.
- `get_states() -> AIStateBase[]`: Every state, in the order they're checked.
- `update_state(_tick: int) -> void`: `AIManager.think()` calls this at each decision. Checks the states in order and moves to the first that fits.

## AITargetSelector

`res://assets/scripts/ai/AITargetSelector.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Picks the AI's current target from its memory, by priority: the standard threat or aggro table, kept small.

A component of the pawn's AIManager. At each decision, before the state, every memory entry at `min_awareness` or more is a candidate; the highest priority wins (ties: the nearer, then the lower id) and becomes the context's current_target, which gets a fading bonus so the pawn doesn't flick between two close targets. A taunt is threat on the taunter's entry (no forcing).

```gdscript
priority = awareness_weight × awareness
         + distance_weight × (1 − distance / distance_range)     (distance to its last known position)
         + threat_weight × threat
         + current_target_bonus × current_target_fade's value    (only for the current target)
```

A game with its own rules overrides `target_priority()`; the loop then runs in GDScript instead of the memory store (`AIMemoryStore` in C++, whose `best_target` must match this formula). Listen to `target_changed`. Design: pawn spec 10.5, 10.11 and 16.5.

### Settings and properties

- `awareness_weight: float` = `1.0`: How much awareness counts.
- `distance_weight: float` = `0.5`: How much being near counts.
- `threat_weight: float` = `1.0`: How much threat counts.
- `distance_range: float` = `25.0`: Distance, in metres, at which nearness counts for nothing. Usually the sight range.
- `min_awareness: float` = `0.3`: Entries below this awareness aren't targets, so a barely noticed shape isn't chased.
- `current_target_bonus: float` = `0.3`: Added to the current target's priority, fading by current_target_fade.
- `current_target_fade: FadeProfile`: How the current target bonus fades. Empty: full for 60 ticks, then a straight line to nothing over 60 more.
- `pawn: Pawn` = `null`: The pawn this is a part of, or null.

### Signals

- `target_changed(old_target: Node3D, new_target: Node3D, reason: String)`: Sent once each time the current target changes. Either can be null.

### Functions

- `get_current_target() -> Node3D`: The current target, or null.
- `update_target(tick: int) -> void`: `AIManager.think()` calls this at each decision, before the state is checked.
- `target_priority(memory: AIMemory, index: int, tick: int) -> float`: This entry's target priority. Override for a game's own rules.

## FadeProfile

`res://assets/scripts/ai/FadeProfile.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

How a value fades over ticks, from full to nothing, as a Resource designers tune in the inspector.

Used by memory's awareness and the target selector's current target bonus. One profile has one curve (`Mode`): LINEAR, HALF_LIFE (counts as nothing below 1%) or CURVE (a drawn curve). Its tick settings are written for 60 a second and used at the match's rate (`TickDriver.ticks_at_rate`). For a fade no mode covers, extend it and override `value_at()` and `ends_after()`; the C++ memory store then calls it, and the C++ decider hands that pawn to GDScript.

```gdscript
var fade := FadeProfile.new()  # or a .tres file made in the inspector, shared by everything that uses it
fade.value_at(30)              # 1.0 at the start, falling to 0.0
fade.ends_after()              # ticks until it's nothing; from then on value_at() gives exactly 0.0
```

Design: pawn spec 10.2.

### Settings and properties

- `mode: int` = `0`: Which curve the fade follows. See the class description.
- `hold_ticks: int` = `0`: Ticks at full strength before the fade begins.
- `fade_ticks: int` = `60`: LINEAR and CURVE: ticks from full to nothing, after the hold.
- `half_life_ticks: int` = `30`: HALF_LIFE: the value halves every this many ticks, after the hold.
- `curve: Curve`: CURVE: the shape of the fade. x runs from 0 (the end of the hold) to 1 (fade_ticks later); y is the value.

### Constants

- `Mode.LINEAR = 0`
- `Mode.HALF_LIFE = 1`
- `Mode.CURVE = 2`
- `HALVINGS_UNTIL_NOTHING = 7`

### Functions

- `values_at_rate() -> Dictionary`: Its settings as plain data at the match's tick rate: mode, hold, fade, half_life (ticks) and curve. Twin: the C++ decider's `fade_math.h` does the same maths as `value_at()`.
- `value_at(ticks: float) -> float`: The value this many ticks after the fade started: 1.0 at the start, falling to 0.0. ticks can be fractional and are real ticks at the match's rate. A tick below 0 gives 1.0.
- `ends_after() -> int`: Ticks from the start until the value is nothing. From then on, value_at() gives exactly 0.0.

## AIAttackBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIAttackBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Attacks the current target once it's close enough: a swing, a shot, any attack on its action.

Allowed in Combat. Available when the target's last known position is within the attack's reach (`AbilityBase.attack_reach()` of the ability on `AIBehaviourDefinition.presses_action`) minus `AIAttackDefinition.approach_margin`: the AI steps a little closer than the real reach so the attack lands. Chase brings the pawn in (score 0.8); this scores 0.9 and takes over at that distance. It faces the target, holds the attack's action through the attack, sleeps until it ends, then finishes. Its interrupt_threshold (15) stops an ordinary decision cutting an attack off. A second Attack with another action and a higher score gives a special or ranged attack (the sample goblins' HeavyAttack and Shoot). A `AIAttackDefinition.min_distance` keeps a ranged one from firing at point blank, so the melee attacks take over there ([`AIKeepDistanceBehaviour`](#aikeepdistancebehaviour) hangs back between shots). Design: pawn spec 10.7 (step 9), 8.6, 8.20 and 8.24; scaling spec 6.2.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: Close enough: the target is within the attack's reach - `AIAttackDefinition.approach_margin`, and no nearer than `AIAttackDefinition.min_distance` if that's set. With no attack on presses_action nothing is close enough, so it never runs. If the attack's range changes during play, call `AIBehaviourBase.rebuild_conditions()`.
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIChaseBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIChaseBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Runs after the current target, and stops within reach for Attack to take over.

Allowed in Combat. While the target is seen it gives one persistent order, `AIController.follow()`: the controller closes in on the target, repathing every `AIChaseDefinition.repath_ticks` or when the target moves `AIChaseDefinition.repath_distance`, stops within `AIChaseDefinition.stop_distance` and faces it for Attack. Once the target hasn't been seen for `AIChaseDefinition.lost_after_ticks` it walks to where it was last seen instead. It holds sprint throughout; with `AIChaseDefinition.dash_to_close` on it also dashes to close the last few metres. It never finishes on its own: when the target is out of sight long enough, Combat's prerequisites fail and the state change replaces it. Orders only when one of those changes, so an order stream carries a few per chase, not one a tick (netcode spec 19.10). Design: pawn spec 10.7.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIGoToPointBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIGoToPointBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Walks to a meeting point: the nearest node in a Godot group, "rally_point" by default.

Allowed in Idle, scoring just above Wander (0.15 against 0.1), so an idle pawn marches to the point, anything it notices on the way takes over, and on arrival Wander takes over. Available while a node is in `AIGoToPointDefinition.point_group` and the pawn is further than `AIGoToPointDefinition.arrive_radius` from it (the nearest is looked up every 2 seconds, `AIInputs.nearest_in_group()`). It walks in legs of at most `AIGoToPointDefinition.leg_metres`, each a move_to, because nav is only built near streaming sources; a leg that can't be walked is retried shorter. Each pawn walks a little to one side of the line (up to `AIGoToPointDefinition.spread_metres`, from its random numbers) so a crowd marches as a band. It never finishes on its own: it stops being available once the pawn has arrived. Design: scaling spec 6.2.

### Constants

- `SIDE_SALT = 24737`

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: A node is in point_group, and the pawn is further than arrive_radius from the nearest one: two conditions.
- `enter(_context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIInvestigateBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIInvestigateBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Walks over to see what something half-noticed was.

Allowed in Alert. Available while the most aware memory entry isn't certain yet (Search handles certain ones), or while an unknown attacker hit the pawn within `AIInvestigateDefinition.hit_memory_ticks`, when it walks to where the hit came from. It walks, without sprinting, to the entry's last known position and heads for a new one if that moves more than `AIInvestigateDefinition.repath_distance`. It succeeds on arriving and fails if there's no way there; its cooldown stops it walking to the same spot over and over. Design: pawn spec 10.7.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: Only for something half-noticed: an uncertain most aware entry, or a recent hit from an attacker it doesn't remember. Either will do.
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIKeepDistanceBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIKeepDistanceBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Hangs back at shooting distance from the current target: a ranged pawn's way of moving in a fight, in place of Chase.

Allowed in Combat while a ranged attack has shots left (the status.has_ammo.ranged tag). Available only to a pawn with a ranged attack (an ability in `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.ranged_tag`'s group with a reach, `AbilityBase.attack_reach()`), and only while the target is at least `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.melee_distance` away. While the target is seen it gives one persistent order, `AIController.keep_distance()`: the controller keeps `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.reach_fraction` of that attack's reach from it, closing in or backing away, and stands facing it. Once the target hasn't been seen for `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.lost_after_ticks` it walks to that distance from where it was last seen. Scored 0.85, above Chase (0.8), so a ranged pawn hangs back instead of running in; the Shoot behaviour (an [`AIAttackBehaviour`](#aiattackbehaviour) on the ranged attack's action, scored higher) fires whenever the shot is ready. Once the target closes within melee_distance it isn't available, so Chase and the melee attacks take over; give Shoot the same distance as its `AIAttackDefinition.min_distance` so the pawn melees rather than shooting at point blank. Design: pawn spec 8.24.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: Has a ranged attack, and the target is at least `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.melee_distance` away: one condition. With no ranged attack the condition can never pass. If its abilities change during play, call `AIBehaviourBase.rebuild_conditions()`.
- `preferred_distance() -> float`: The metres from the target it stands at: `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.reach_fraction` of its ranged attack's reach; 0 without one.
- `find_ranged_attack() -> AbilityBase`: The pawn's ranged attack: the first ability in `AIKeepDistanceDefinition.ranged_tag`'s group with a reach, found once. Null if it has none.
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AILookTowardBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AILookTowardBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Stops and looks toward something half-noticed: the first reaction to a glimpse.

Allowed in Alert. Available while the most aware memory entry isn't certain yet, or an unknown attacker hit the pawn within `AILookTowardDefinition.hit_memory_ticks` (then it looks where the hit came from). It stops the pawn and looks at that position for `AILookTowardDefinition.look_ticks`; looking turns the AI's eyes, so a target still in view keeps filling awareness. It scores 0.6, above Investigate (0.5), because turning to look is the cheaper way to become certain; as it starts it gives itself -0.3 for 15 s (`AIBehaviourDefinition.modifier_on_start`), dropping it to 0.3, so Investigate wins and Look Toward doesn't catch again while it walks over. It runs again only when Investigate is cooling down. Design: pawn spec 10.7.

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: Only for something half-noticed: an uncertain most aware entry, or a recent hit from an attacker it doesn't remember. Either will do.
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIParryBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIParryBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Parries a swing coming at the pawn, some of the time (`AIParryDefinition.parry_chance`).

Available when a noted swing hasn't hit yet, its attacker is alive, and this swing's roll came up (two conditions). An enemy's A MeleeAttackAbility (or a fired projectile, FireProjectileStep) tells the AI of an attack when it starts, on the server (`AIManager.note_incoming_attack()`), which asks for a decision at once: ordinary decisions come every 15 ticks, longer than a swing's windup. The roll comes from the swing's start tick and the attacker's pawn number, so each swing is rolled once and a replay rolls the same. It looks at the attacker and presses parry (`AIBehaviourDefinition.presses_action`, so it's skipped while the parry is cooling down or locked out), finishes two ticks later and forgets the swing; ParryAbility does the rest. Design: scaling spec 6.2.

### Constants

- `ROLL_SALT = 39492`

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: A swing is coming, and its roll came up: once per swing, from its start tick and its attacker's number.
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AISearchBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AISearchBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Hunts around where an enemy it became certain of was last seen: "I know you were here".

Allowed in Alert. Available only when the most aware memory entry is certain but not fresh enough for Combat (Look Toward and Investigate handle half-noticed things). It goes to the last known position (holding sprint if `AISearchDefinition.sprint_to_last_known` is on), then walks to `AISearchDefinition.search_points` random points within `AISearchDefinition.search_radius` of it, standing `AISearchDefinition.pause_ticks` at each, and succeeds. While still Alert it's usually picked again, so it keeps searching until the entry fades (Idle) or the enemy is seen (Combat). Design: pawn spec 10.7.

### Constants

- `POINT_ANGLE_SALT = 24225`
- `POINT_DISTANCE_SALT = 24226`

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `own_conditions() -> AICondition[]`: Only for an enemy it became certain of: the most aware entry in memory exists and is certain. Its score is always max_score.
- `enter(context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIWanderBehaviour

`res://assets/scripts/ai/behaviours/AIWanderBehaviour.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourBase`](#aibehaviourbase)

Walks to random nearby points, pausing between them: what a pawn does when nothing more interesting can run.

Allowed in Idle, with a low fixed score. It picks a random point within `AIWanderDefinition.wander_radius` of its home (where the pawn first started wandering), walks there with the AI controller's move_to, then stands for a random time between `AIWanderDefinition.min_pause_ticks` and `AIWanderDefinition.max_pause_ticks`. The points and pauses come from the context's replayable random numbers, so the same seed, pawn and ticks give the same walk. A point with no way there is skipped and another tried soon. It never finishes on its own. Design: pawn spec 10.7.

### Constants

- `POINT_ANGLE_SALT = 20897`
- `POINT_DISTANCE_SALT = 20898`
- `PAUSE_SALT = 20899`

### Functions

- `make_default_definition() -> AIBehaviourDefinition`
- `enter(_context: AIManager) -> void`
- `tick(context: AIManager) -> int`
- `exit(context: AIManager, _reason: String) -> void`

## AIAnyCondition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/conditions/AIAnyCondition.gd`, extends [`AICondition`](#aicondition)

A condition that passes if any one of its conditions passes: "this, or that".

A behaviour's own list of conditions needs all of them; this is how to say "or" (Look Toward: something half-noticed, or an unknown attacker hit lately). The conditions are checked in order and it stops at the first that passes; an empty list never passes. Design: scaling spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `conditions: AICondition[]` = `[]`: Passes if any one of these does.

### Functions

- `make(list: AICondition[]) -> AIAnyCondition` *(static)*: Makes an "any of" condition in code.
- `passes(inputs: AIInputs, context: AIManager, behaviour_salt: int) -> bool`
- `describe() -> Dictionary`
- `add_input_slots(slots: Dictionary) -> void`

## AIChanceCondition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/conditions/AIChanceCondition.gd`, extends [`AICondition`](#aicondition)

A condition that passes on a random roll, with a chance from 0 to 1, the same roll on every run.

The roll comes from `AIManager.random_unit_at()` (pawn, tick, salt), rolled again at every decision by default. With `once_per_input` set, that input's value takes the tick's place, so the roll holds until the input changes: Parry rolls once per swing. The C++ decider rolls the same hash, so both give the same answer.

```gdscript
chance 0.3, once_per_input incoming_attack_tick, salt_input incoming_attacker   # 30%, once per swing
```

Design: scaling spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `chance: float` = `0.5`: How likely it is to pass, from 0 (never) to 1 (always).
- `salt: int` = `0`: What the roll is for. Two chance conditions on one behaviour need different salts, or they'd roll the same number.
- `once_per_input: String` = `""`: Optional: roll once per value of this input instead of once per decision, such as incoming_attack_tick for once per swing.
- `salt_input: String` = `""`: Optional: an input mixed into the salt, such as incoming_attacker, so two swings that start on the same tick roll differently.

### Functions

- `make(passing_chance: float, salt_number: int, once_per: StringName = &"", mixed_in: StringName = &"") -> AIChanceCondition` *(static)*: Makes a chance condition in code.
- `passes(inputs: AIInputs, context: AIManager, behaviour_salt: int) -> bool`
- `roll_tick(inputs: AIInputs, now: int) -> int`: The tick the roll is made for: the decision's, or `once_per_input`'s value.
- `roll_salt(inputs: AIInputs, behaviour_salt: int) -> int`: The salt the roll is made with: `salt`, the behaviour's own number and `salt_input`'s value (its low 16 bits).
- `describe() -> Dictionary`
- `add_input_slots(slots: Dictionary) -> void`

## AICompareCondition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/conditions/AICompareCondition.gd`, extends [`AICondition`](#aicondition)

A condition that compares one input with a number, or with another input plus a number.

Inputs that are yes or no are 1 or 0, so compare them with EQUAL 1 or EQUAL 0. Design: scaling spec 6.2. Examples:

```gdscript
target_distance  AT_MOST  2.5                           # the target is within 2.5 m
most_aware_certain  EQUAL  1                            # the AI is certain about what it's most aware of
ticks_since_unknown_hit  AT_MOST  300                   # hit by someone unknown within 5 s (ticks at 60 a second)
target_distance  AT_MOST  -0.5, other_input "reach"     # within the "reach" input minus half a metre
```

### Settings and properties

- `input: String` = `""`: The input to check, such as target_distance. See [`AIInputs`](#aiinputs) for the built-in ones.
- `comparison: int` = `0`: How it's compared.
- `value: float` = `0.0`: The number it's compared with. For an input that's a time in ticks (its name starts with ticks_), written for 60 ticks a second. With `other_input` set, it's added to that input's value instead.
- `other_input: String` = `""`: Optional: compare with this input's value plus `value`, instead of with value alone.

### Constants

- `Comparison.AT_MOST = 0`: input <= value
- `Comparison.LESS_THAN = 1`: input < value
- `Comparison.AT_LEAST = 2`: input >= value
- `Comparison.MORE_THAN = 3`: input > value
- `Comparison.EQUAL = 4`: input == value
- `Comparison.NOT_EQUAL = 5`: input != value

### Functions

- `make(input_name: StringName, how: int, number: float, other_name: StringName = &"") -> AICompareCondition` *(static)*: Makes a compare condition in code: AICompareCondition.make(AIInputs.TARGET_DISTANCE, AICompareCondition.Comparison.AT_MOST, 2.5).
- `passes(inputs: AIInputs, _context: AIManager, _behaviour_salt: int) -> bool`
- `describe() -> Dictionary`
- `add_input_slots(slots: Dictionary) -> void`

## AICondition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/conditions/AICondition.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

The base for a condition: one check a behaviour needs to pass before it may run, made of plain data.

A behaviour runs only while all its conditions pass (`AIBehaviourBase.all_conditions()`). A condition reads named numbers from the pawn's [`AIInputs`](#aiinputs), never game objects, so the C++ decider (`AIDecider`) can make the same check for a crowd. The kinds, each a Resource made in the inspector, are [`AICompareCondition`](#aicomparecondition), [`AIChanceCondition`](#aichancecondition) and [`AIAnyCondition`](#aianycondition). A new kind needs the same check in C++ (native/src/ai_decider.cpp) and a `describe()` giving what C++ reads; most needs are met by a game writing its own input (`AIInputs.set_input()`) instead. Design: scaling spec 6.2.

### Constants

- `CPP_KINDS = Array[String](["always", "compare", "chance", "any"])`: The kinds the C++ decider reads (`describe()`'s "kind"). A behaviour with a condition of another kind is judged in GDScript.
