- `INPUT_SUGGESTIONS = "target_distance,most_aware_certain,most_aware_uncertain,ticks_since_unknown_hit,incoming_attack,incoming_attack_tick,incoming_attacker,group_distance/rally_point,group_found/rally_point,action_ready/primary"`: The input names the inspector suggests. Any other name works too: it's a kept input that game code writes.

### Functions

- `passes(_inputs: AIInputs, _context: AIManager, _behaviour_salt: int) -> bool`: True if the condition passes for this pawn now. inputs holds the values worked out for this decision; behaviour_salt is the behaviour's own number for random rolls, so two behaviours' rolls differ.
- `describe() -> Dictionary`: The condition as plain data, for the C++ decider: "kind" and its numbers, with input slots (`AIInputs.slot_of()`) rather than names, and times already converted to the match's tick rate.
- `add_input_slots(_slots: Dictionary) -> void`: Adds the slots of every input this condition reads to slots (as keys), so the behaviour manager works out only those.
- `cpp_reads(described: Dictionary) -> bool` *(static)*: True if the C++ decider reads this described condition (`describe()`) and every condition inside it.
- `at_rate_for(slot: int, number: float) -> float` *(static)*: A value written for 60 ticks a second, at the match's rate, if the input is a time in ticks; otherwise the value as it is.

## AIScoreCurve

`res://assets/scripts/ai/conditions/AIScoreCurve.gd`, extends [`Resource`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_resource.html)

Turns one input into an amount from 0 to 1 that scales a behaviour's score: the "how much" to a condition's "whether".

Scaling spec 6.2. A straight line: `from_value` gives 0, `to_value` gives 1, with 0 below and 1 above. Set to_value below from_value to turn it round (more input, less score). A behaviour's score is `low + (max_score - low) × every curve's amount multiplied together`, where low is min_score, or 0 when min_score isn't set (`AIBehaviourBase.score()`). With no curves the score is max_score.

```gdscript
target_distance, from 20 to 2     # 0 at 20 m or further, 1 at 2 m or closer: the nearer, the keener
```

### Settings and properties

- `input: String` = `""`: The input it reads, such as target_distance. See [`AIInputs`](#aiinputs).
- `from_value: float` = `0.0`: The input value that gives 0. For a time in ticks, written for 60 ticks a second.
- `to_value: float` = `1.0`: The input value that gives 1.

### Functions

- `make(input_name: StringName, zero_at: float, one_at: float) -> AIScoreCurve` *(static)*: Makes a curve in code.
- `amount(inputs: AIInputs) -> float`: The amount from 0 to 1 for this pawn's inputs now.
- `describe() -> Dictionary`: The curve as plain data, for the C++ decider, with times converted to the match's rate.
- `add_input_slots(slots: Dictionary) -> void`: Adds the slot of the input it reads to slots (as a key).

## AIAttackDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/definitions/AIAttackDefinition.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourDefinition`](#aibehaviourdefinition)

The settings of a Attack behaviour ([`AIAttackBehaviour`](#aiattackbehaviour)), shared by every pawn whose Attack uses it.

Its kind's own settings below; the ones every behaviour has come from [`AIBehaviourDefinition`](#aibehaviourdefinition). A new one starts with the defaults Attack runs with when it has no definition.

### Settings and properties

- `approach_margin: float` = `0.3`: How much closer than the attack's range the AI steps before attacking, in metres.
- `min_distance: float` = `0.0`: The nearest the target may be for this attack, in metres; 0: no limit. For a ranged attack, set it to the Keep Distance behaviour's melee_distance, so a target that close is met with melee instead.

## AIBehaviourDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/definitions/AIBehaviourDefinition.gd`, extends [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition)

The settings one variant of an AI behaviour has, shared by every pawn that uses it, such as "Goblin Chase": a Resource a behaviour node points at (pawn spec 16.3).

Each kind of behaviour has its own class with its settings added ([`AIChaseDefinition`](#aichasedefinition)); a new one starts with the kind's defaults. Variants (`Definition.based_on`) come from [`Definition`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#definition). Read-only while playing: every pawn using it shares it. A pawn that needs other numbers uses another definition (`AIBehaviourBase.use_definition()`) or a behaviour modifier.

### Settings and properties

- `tags: StringName[]` = `[]`: What it is, as tags such as &"ai.stance.melee": what behaviour modifiers pick behaviours by (`AIBehaviourModifier.applies_to`).
- `tag_requirements: TagQuery`: When it may run: a query over the pawn's owned tags, such as any of ai.state.combat (the AI's state is a tag), or none of status.has_ammo. While it fails, the behaviour can't be chosen, and a running one is replaced at the next AI step. Empty: always.
- `max_score: float` = `0.5`: The highest its score can be. Lets the manager skip it without running its code when it can't win.
- `min_score: float` = `inf_neg`: Optional: the lowest its score can be. Left at -inf it can't help skip others, but it's never wrong.
- `needs_target: bool` = `false`: Skipped while the AI has no current target.
- `presses_action: StringName` = `&""`: A named action it presses, such as &"primary". Skipped while that action couldn't start.
- `conditions: AICondition[]` = `[]`: More conditions it needs, on top of its kind's own (`AIBehaviourBase.own_conditions()`). All must pass. Made in the inspector: compare an input with a number, a random chance, or "any of".
- `score_curves: AIScoreCurve[]` = `[]`: Optional: inputs that scale its score between min_score (or 0) and max_score, multiplied together. Empty: always max_score.
- `cooldown_ticks: int` = `0`: Ticks after it ends before it can be chosen again. A hard rule, checked before any scoring.
- `min_run_ticks: int` = `0`: Once chosen, ordinary decisions can't replace it for this many ticks. State changes still can, if strong enough. Behaviour modifiers can change it, as they can cooldown_ticks, interrupt_threshold and score_jitter.
- `interrupt_threshold: int` = `0`: While it runs, only events of this priority or higher can replace it: 0 for an ordinary decision, a state's priority for a state change. 0: anything can.
- `cannot_be_interrupted: bool` = `false`: Runs until it returns SUCCEEDED or FAILED, whatever happens, even if its state no longer allows it. Use sparingly.
- `score_jitter: float` = `-1.0`: ± random offset on its score at each decision, for variety. -1: the manager's default_score_jitter.
- `tick_interval_ticks: int` = `1`: While it runs, its tick() is called every this many ticks, and sooner when a wake-up it asked for happens (the longest it sleeps). 1: every tick.
- `modifier_on_start: AIBehaviourModifier`: A modifier it gives itself as it starts, such as a score bonus that keeps it chosen a while. Empty applies_to: only this behaviour. With no duration it lasts while the behaviour runs; with one, its duration from the start. Starting again replaces it.
- `modifier_on_end: AIBehaviourModifier`: A modifier it gives itself as it ends, such as -0.3 to its score for 15 s so something else gets a turn. Empty applies_to: only this behaviour. With no duration it lasts until the behaviour starts again; with one, its duration. Ending again replaces it.

## AIChaseDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/definitions/AIChaseDefinition.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourDefinition`](#aibehaviourdefinition)

The settings of a Chase behaviour ([`AIChaseBehaviour`](#aichasebehaviour)), shared by every pawn whose Chase uses it.

Its kind's own settings below; the ones every behaviour has come from [`AIBehaviourDefinition`](#aibehaviourdefinition). A new one starts with the defaults Chase runs with when it has no definition.

### Settings and properties

- `repath_ticks: int` = `20`: Ticks between new paths.
- `repath_distance: float` = `1.5`: How far, in metres, the target must move from where the path leads before a new path is found early.
- `lost_after_ticks: int` = `30`: Ticks since the target was last seen after which it's chased to where it was last seen, not where it is (at 60 a second).
- `stop_distance: float` = `1.2`: How close, in metres, it gets before stopping.
- `sprint: bool` = `true`: On: it holds sprint while chasing. Sprint's own cooldown decides when it actually sprints.
- `dash_to_close: bool` = `false`: On: it presses dash to close in, when the target is between `dash_to_distance` and `dash_from_distance` away and the ability can start (in the air too, Dash's usable_in_air). Off by default. A dash goes the way the pawn is moving, along its path.
- `close_in_tag: StringName` = `&"ability.movement.advanced"`: The group of ability it uses to close in, not one ability by name: any ability tagged with it that can start (`AbilityManager.action_for_tag()`). Advanced movement by default.
- `dash_from_distance: float` = `7.5`: The farthest the target can be for a dash, in metres.
- `dash_to_distance: float` = `5.5`: The nearest the target can be for a dash, in metres. A dash from a sprint (9 m/s) covers about 4.2 m, so 5.5 lands it a little outside stop_distance.

## AIKeepDistanceDefinition

`res://assets/scripts/ai/definitions/AIKeepDistanceDefinition.gd`, extends [`AIBehaviourDefinition`](#aibehaviourdefinition)

The settings of a Keep Distance behaviour ([`AIKeepDistanceBehaviour`](#aikeepdistancebehaviour)), shared by every pawn whose Keep Distance uses it.

- `repath_distance: float` = `1.5`: How far, in metres, the spot it walks to must move before a new path is found early.

## SightGeometryFeeder

`res://assets/scripts/ai/senses/SightGeometryFeeder.gd`, extends [`RefCounted`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_refcounted.html)

Keeps the shared SightGeometry (line of sight in C++) fed with the solid things in the scene.

With the geometry fed, line of sight can be tested off the main thread instead of with physics rays. On first use it finds every body in the tree, then follows the tree (a body entering or leaving, a collision shape added to or removed from a body); anything else the geometry notices itself, once a tick. So a designer only puts a prop on a layer in sight's sight_blocking_mask (layer 1 by default) and it blocks sight. Areas and pawns are left out. Never instanced: everything is static, so no autoload is needed. Design: scaling spec step 4.

### Settings and properties

- `enabled: bool` = `true`: Off: no geometry, so sight casts physics rays on the main thread. Read when sight is first used; set it before pawns are made.

### Functions

- `get_geometry() -> Object` *(static)*: The shared geometry, or null without the C++ library or with enabled off.

## SightSense

`res://assets/scripts/ai/senses/SightSense.gd`, extends [`AISenseBase`](#aisensebase)

Sight, for basic stealth: fills awareness of other-team pawns it can see, faster when they're close and in front.

A child of the pawn's [`AISensingManager`](#aisensingmanager). For each other-team pawn it checks, on a full pass or a refresh:

```gdscript
if there's no line of sight: no gain
gain = fill_rate × ticks_since_last_check × distance_factor × angle_factor × the target's detectability (its stat)
```

Ticks since the last check (capped at `max_gain_ticks`) make the checking rate not matter; the distance factor is 1 inside `near_range` and falls to 0 at `sight_range`; the angle factor is 1 in the central cone, `periphery_multiplier` in the periphery, 0 outside. Line of sight is one ray from the eyes to the target, blocked only by `sight_blocking_mask`. The eyes face where the AI is looking, else the way the body faces (where the player looks while one has the pawn). The checks run in the pawn's memory store (`AIMemoryStore` in C++, else [`AIMemoryStoreGD`](#aimemorystoregd)); with C++ the ray is tested against [`SightGeometryFeeder`](#sightgeometryfeeder)'s geometry, on worker threads when the sensing job runs. Refreshes check only the current target. Design: pawn spec 10.4, scaling spec step 4.

### Settings and properties

- `fill_rate: float` = `0.03333333333333333`: Awareness a fully visible target adds per tick: 1/30 fills it in 30 ticks, half a second. Per tick at 60 a second; at another rate it's converted to fill at the same speed.
- `near_range: float` = `8.0`: Inside this distance, in metres, distance doesn't weaken sight at all.
- `sight_range: float` = `25.0`: Beyond this distance, in metres, nothing is seen.
- `central_cone_degrees: float` = `90.0`: The width of the central cone, in degrees, where sight is at full strength.
- `periphery_degrees: float` = `160.0`: The width of everything it can see, in degrees, the central cone included. The part outside the central cone is the periphery.
- `periphery_multiplier: float` = `0.3`: How strongly the periphery sees, compared with the central cone.
- `max_gain_ticks: int` = `30`: The most ticks one check can count, so a long gap doesn't give a huge gain at once.
- `eye_height: float` = `1.6`: The height of the eyes above the pawn's feet, in metres.
- `target_height: float` = `1.0`: The height on the target the ray aims at, in metres above its feet: about the chest.
- `sight_blocking_mask: int` = `1`: Physics layers that block sight. The world, layer 1, by default.

### Functions

- `get_range() -> float`: Its `sight_range`.
- `full_pass(candidates: Pawn[], tick: int) -> void`: The whole pass runs in memory's store (C++ when available, else GDScript), with this sense's settings.
- `full_pass_prepared(job: Object, tick: int) -> void`: The full pass with the sensing job's result: the job found the candidates, how visible each is and (against SightGeometry) the line of sight, on a worker thread; this records them, the same as full_pass would. AISensingManager calls it.
- `ask_job(job: Object, reach: float, max_candidates: int) -> void`: Asks the sensing job for next tick's full pass, with where the eyes face now and this sense's settings.
- `refresh(tick: int) -> void`: Only the current target, one ray. Refreshing every remembered entity costs more than the full passes in a crowd (measured with ai_stress), and keeping a tracked target fresh is what the refresh is for.
- `visibility_of(target: Pawn) -> float`: How strongly this pawn would see the target now, before line of sight and the time factor: distance × angle × detectability. 0 when it's out of range or outside the periphery. Public so tests and debug readouts can show it.
- `has_line_of_sight(target: Pawn) -> bool`: True if nothing in sight_blocking_mask is between the eyes and the target.

## AIAwarenessState

`res://assets/scripts/ai/states/AIAwarenessState.gd`, extends [`AIStateBase`](#aistatebase)

One tunable state for every "how aware am I of an enemy" situation, such as Alert and Combat.

The default Alert and Combat are two nodes running this script with different settings, so a designer makes a new awareness state by adding a node and filling in the settings, with no code. Its prerequisites hold when the entry it looks at (the current target, or any entry in memory) meets `min_awareness`, `requires_certain` and `max_ticks_since_seen`, or separately when the pawn was hit within `hit_within_ticks` by an `attacker` of the right kind. So Combat holds when a known attacker hits, and Alert when an unknown one does (there is no damage sense). Design: pawn spec 10.6.

### Settings and properties

- `looks_at: int` = `1`: Which entries it looks at.
- `min_awareness: float` = `0.3`: Awareness it needs, 0 to 1.
- `requires_certain: bool` = `false`: On: only entries that became certain count.
- `max_ticks_since_seen: int` = `-1`: Only entries seen within this many ticks (at 60 a second) count. -1: any time.
- `hit_within_ticks: int` = `-1`: Or the pawn was hit within this many ticks (at 60 a second), by an attacker of the kind below. -1: off.
- `attacker: int` = `0`: Which attackers count for hit_within_ticks.

### Constants

- `LooksAt.CURRENT_TARGET = 0`: the target the target selector picked
- `LooksAt.ANY_ENTRY = 1`: any entry in memory
- `Attacker.ANY = 0`: any attacker
- `Attacker.KNOWN = 1`: one the pawn has in memory
- `Attacker.UNKNOWN = 2`: one it doesn't

### Functions

- `prerequisites_met(context: AIManager) -> bool`

## AIIdleState

`res://assets/scripts/ai/states/AIIdleState.gd`, extends [`AIStateBase`](#aistatebase)

The state for when nothing else fits: its prerequisites always hold.

It has the lowest priority and catches every case the other states don't. Every state manager should have one, or there are moments when no state fits. Design: pawn spec 10.6.

### Functions

- `prerequisites_met(_context: AIManager) -> bool`
